## opencode {VERSION}

{Prerelease/Stable} release from `{branch}` branch. Explicit request header overrides now survive transport boundaries under Bun, and the native runtime keeps internal title-routing markers away from ordinary OAuth fetches.

---

### 🐛 Bug Fixes

- **Preserve request header overrides at transport boundaries**: After internal title-marker cleanup, an explicit header override could become empty, and Bun then rebuilt the outgoing Request with the original headers, restoring Authorization, private headers, or the title marker the caller had replaced. Provider, WebSocket-pool HTTP, and OAuth-to-API HTTP transports now apply the effective sanitized headers, rebuilding the native Request only when needed, while keeping native body sources, signal overrides, 307/308 redirect replay, custom fetch priority, and registered title consumers. The provider header timeout is also cleared when request preparation or a custom fetch throws synchronously (#748).
- **Strip title markers before ordinary native OAuth fetches**: The experimental native runtime kept the internal `x-opencode-title` marker whenever an OpenAI OAuth provider supplied any fetch. It now keeps the marker only for registered OpenCode transports that consume it, matching the AI SDK provider boundary (#750).

### 🔍 Verification

The header-override suite added 15 regressions that failed on the v1.0.71 implementation, alongside 8 passing controls, and covers record, Headers, and tuple overrides, inherited headers, native body and cancellation behavior, redirects, and timeout cleanup. The native-runtime regression failed before its fix and passed after it, while existing OAuth title-routing and direct native HTTP regressions continued to pass. An independent review of the merged WebSocket transport work and both fixes found no blocking defects. Native CI evidence is maintained in each PR and checked on the final head before merge.
